value.rationale: The endpoint norm of a consecutive Fourier projection is the canonical discrete Lebesgue constant. A single all-length formula and a complete residue-class second-order law organize and extend isolated small-block evaluations, while reducing the exact computation for fixed m from an N-sample absolute sum to a bounded number of elementary trigonometric terms. The invariant and the finite-to-continuous sampling defect are mathematically natural and reusable.
